# keyrx

> Solana and EVM vanity address grinder. One seed, many addresses, exact keys and paths. Offline grinding. Open. Verified. The mark is a record. What it seals comes next.
>
> One seed phrase is a tree of addresses; keyrx
> derives the expensive prefix once and walks the account index. In the cited
> measurements it reached 19.5-32.2x aggregate throughput and 33-55x per core
> versus `solana-keygen grind --use-mnemonic`. Every Solana match writes
> the address, its derivation path, the seed phrase, a base58 keypair for current
> Phantom/Solflare private-key import flows, and a JSON byte array for
> solana-keygen. One Rust binary. No daemon or service. Grinding, estimating,
> benchmarking, showing and verifying are offline; explicit --update may use Cargo's network access.
>
> `--chain evm` (0.4.0): Ethereum and every EVM chain - the same mnemonic walk on
> secp256k1 at m/44'/60'/0'/0/N, keccak addresses in EIP-55 case; hex patterns,
> any case by default, `--checksum` for EIP-55 case as typed; the match writes the
> 0x hex private key MetaMask and Rabby import. Matches under matches/evm/.

The site is a terminal UI rendered in JavaScript with a suffix probability
demo in a Web Worker: random 32-byte values, real base58 encoding, and no
keypair, seed, signer or derivation path. Nothing leaves the browser. This
file carries the same product content as plain text.

## Install

Linux x86-64 has one prebuilt release archive; Windows runs the same Linux binary inside WSL:

    keyrx-<version>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz

Download it and its matching `.tar.gz.sha256` sidecar from the same GitHub Release, verify the
archive, extract it, install `keyrx` into `${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin`, then run `keyrx verify`.
The release's
`keyrx-<version>.SHA256SUMS` separately inventories every other attached asset.

    export PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH"
    keyrx verify                 # run first, always: base58, derivation, the pinned solana-keygen answer, the BIP39 passphrase vector

There is no native Windows binary. There are no macOS archives until signed and notarized Apple
silicon and Intel binaries exist. macOS and source-build users install Rust 1.85 or newer from the
official rustup instructions at https://rustup.rs/, then:

    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
    export PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH"
    rustup default stable
    cargo install --locked keyrx
    keyrx verify

Ubuntu's suggested `apt install cargo` can be below Rust 1.85. Distro rustup packages are not the
tested upstream-rustup path. The PATH remedy does not assume `~/.cargo/env` exists. From a clone:

    git clone https://github.com/keyrx/keyrx && cd keyrx
    RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native" cargo install --locked --path .  # POSIX shell; tuned to this CPU

Then use the tool:

    keyrx                       # the start screen
    keyrx bench --indices 128    # this machine's measured 128-index workload; estimate uses it
    keyrx estimate --ends-with KEYRX --indices 128 --count 10    # odds; measured time to one and all ten
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --indices 128    # writes one .md and prints its exact show command
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --count 10       # ten matches, one Markdown file per hit
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --indices 8      # keep seed-path discovery bounded; verify the printed path
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --passphrase     # BIP39 passphrase: prompted, hidden, never stored; import that address by key
    keyrx grind --starts-with Key --ends-with RX   # both ends; --ignore-case for any case (32x likelier for five letters)
    keyrx show                   # every Markdown record and legacy ledger; prints each exact show command
    keyrx --update               # Cargo-installed builds update in place; prebuilt users get the release path

`bench`, `grind`, and `show` require Unix owner-only file semantics. On
Windows, run them under WSL. Probability is not machine-specific; a matching
benchmark profile supplies the time estimate. Solana odds are an explicitly approximate base58
model because signing-key outputs are not uniform text. EVM bench uses a rare 16-hex suffix;
estimate labels other matcher shapes as an approximate measured baseline.

## What a match writes

A default grind writes every successful hit as one self-contained, versioned Markdown recovery
record in the mode-0700 managed matches directory; every record is mode 0600 on Unix. It does not
also append the hit to an aggregate file. Its uppercase headings put the exact value on the next
line: ADDRESS, PATH, SEED, PASSPHRASE, and PRIVATE KEY; a Solana record also has KEYPAIR (JSON).
The Solana private key is base58. The EVM private key is 0x-prefixed hex, and an EVM record has no
Solana JSON keypair. Solana and EVM records carry only their own chain-specific import and recovery
guidance.

Every record includes the safe creation recipe. It preserves chain, patterns, case mode, path,
indices, word count, and whether --passphrase was used, but never the passphrase value. Count,
output, terminal display, and worker settings are omitted deliberately. A key import lands on the
exact address as a standalone account; an unrelated wallet seed does not recover it. Seed recovery
depends on the exact printed path and the receiving wallet/version. Verify the address before
funding, and keep every record or an equivalent backup private.

The filename combines the requested lane with the address text that actually matched. For example,
`--ends-with coined --ignore-case` can write `coined.ic.coiNED.md`. If that exact filename already
exists, keyRX creates `coined.ic.coiNED.02.md`, then `.03.md`, with create-new semantics and no
overwrite. Prefix-only and combined prefix/suffix lanes preserve their realized address edges too.
EVM records remain under `matches/evm/`.

After final custody checks, a successful default grind prints one exact copy-ready `keyrx show`
command per record it created. Its full managed path makes it unambiguous from any working
directory; actual case, duplicate suffixes, and the EVM directory are preserved. `--seeds` and
`--keys` are never added automatically.

An explicit `--out FILE` selects the established appendable ledger instead. A new explicit ledger
uses the versioned v1 header and record format; an earlier headerless ledger remains headerless and
append-compatible. Managed Markdown records are never mixed into either ledger form. `keyrx show`
lists and reads both Markdown and ledger formats, with seeds and keys withheld unless `--seeds` or
`--keys` is requested.

## Verified

SLIP-0010 identical to solana-keygen at both path styles (pinned as tests);
ground hits re-derive from their own seed; both key encodings round-trip
through `solana-keygen pubkey` to the same address; 50,000 pubkeys x 10
suffix lengths agree with the full base58 encoding. Bench 24.4x baseline at
128 indices, 32.2x at 256.

MIT. Import and verify the address before funding. Match records and ledgers hold
seed phrases and keys - treat them like a key.
